title: Rajasthan's rural job scheme lacked baseline surveys and district plans, audit finds
dek: An audit of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act in Rajasthan says planning was not grounded in local demand, and it points to staff shortages and missing technical support.
theme: Planning gaps in Rajasthan's rural employment scheme
indiaConnection: This audit examines how a public programme in Rajasthan was carried out and recorded, and it states what the audited record can and cannot establish for the people in India who depend on it.

eventTime.label: Date not established in the supplied evidence

body.text: Between 2019-20 and 2023-24, none of the gram panchayats examined by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in Rajasthan had carried out a baseline survey. As a result, the audit found, it was impossible to determine the nature, volume, or timing of work demand, and no realistic development plan could be drawn up at the grassroots.

No District Perspective Plan had been drawn up in any of the districts that were checked, so the audit could not identify the needs and gaps across all sectors there. Furthermore, in seven selected panchayat samitis, the annual work plans for 16 gram panchayats were made without setting work priorities in the Gram Sabha during the audit period.

The audit says that Block Resource Centres, which were required to provide technical inputs for planning, maintain a database for planning, and ensure convergence between the scheme and other production-oriented programmes, were not set up in any of the selected blocks. This left the gram panchayats without the support system required for planning.

Manpower shortages were found at all levels of the scheme's implementation. The audit reports that regular staff vacancies ranged between 3 per cent and 64 per cent, while contractual staff vacancies ranged between 31 per cent and 80 per cent. It also notes that 100 per cent of the regular Block Resource Persons and Village Resource Persons posts for conducting social audit were vacant, which affected the efficiency of social audits.

The audit looked at the years 2019-20 through 2023-24. Records from 33 districts in Rajasthan were reviewed, but only five were selected for detailed examination, along with 10 panchayat samitis and 40 gram panchayats. In each of those gram panchayats, seven works were chosen for joint physical verification, making 280 in total, and 10 beneficiaries per gram panchayat were surveyed, adding up to 400.

The review aimed to check whether planning and financial management were adequate, how much employment was generated, whether durable and useful assets were created and maintained, and how well the scheme aligned with other initiatives. It also looked at monitoring, social audits, and grievance handling. The audit relied solely on state records, without independent measurements or input from those directly affected.

statements.text: No baseline survey was conducted in any test-checked gram panchayat during 2019-24.
statements.sourceScope: The audit examined records in 40 gram panchayats across five districts in Rajasthan for the period 2019-20 to 2023-24.
statements.limits: The audit does not say whether any baseline survey was done outside the test-checked gram panchayats.

statements.text: No District Perspective Plan was prepared in any test-checked district.
statements.sourceScope: The audit covered five districts in Rajasthan for the period 2019-20 to 2023-24.
statements.limits: The audit does not establish whether district plans existed in other districts or in other years.

statements.text: Annual work plans of 16 selected gram panchayats were prepared without determining priorities in Gram Sabha.
statements.sourceScope: The audit selected 16 gram panchayats from seven panchayat samitis for this review.
statements.limits: The audit does not show how priorities were set in the remaining 24 gram panchayats.

statements.text: Block Resource Centres were not set up in any selected block.
statements.sourceScope: The audit covered 10 panchayat samitis in five districts.
statements.limits: The audit does not state whether BRCs existed in other blocks or what impact their absence had on specific works.

statements.text: Regular staff vacancies ranged from 3 per cent to 64 per cent, and contractual staff vacancies from 31 per cent to 80 per cent.
statements.sourceScope: The audit assessed manpower at state, district, panchayat samiti, and gram panchayat levels during 2019-24.
statements.limits: The audit does not specify which posts had which vacancy rates or how these vacancies affected individual scheme outcomes.

statements.text: All regular Block Resource Persons and Village Resource Persons posts for social audit were vacant.
statements.sourceScope: The audit reviewed social audit staffing in the selected districts and blocks.
statements.limits: The audit does not say whether any alternative arrangements were made for social audits.

statements.text: The audit covered five districts, 10 panchayat samitis, 40 gram panchayats, 280 works, and 400 beneficiaries.
statements.sourceScope: The audit period was 2019-20 to 2023-24, with records examined in the named sample.
statements.limits: The audit does not cover all 33 districts of Rajasthan, so findings may not apply statewide.

statements.text: The audit's findings are based on the state's records and do not include independent measurement or beneficiary perspectives.
statements.sourceScope: The audit relied on official records and physical verification of selected works.
statements.limits: The audit does not provide evidence from independent surveys or direct beneficiary interviews beyond the selected sample.
